q: How much fuel or electricity per tonne should a forging furnace use?
title: Forging furnace energy per tonne benchmark
short: BEE's energy conservation guidelines for MSMEs give 70 to 100 litres of fuel per tonne for fuel-fired forging furnaces and 400 to 600 kWh per tonne for induction forging furnaces. Divide a month's fuel or metered kWh by the tonnes you heated to see where you stand.
audience: Owners and plant heads of forging units running oil, gas or induction furnaces

ul: Fuel-fired: litres of fuel used in the period / tonnes of material heated. For kcal per tonne, multiply fuel kg by its calorific value first.
Induction: kWh from a dedicated meter on the furnace / tonnes heated. BEE asks for a meter reading every batch.
Air ratio: 1.15 to 1.20 on liquid fuel, 1.12 to 1.15 on natural gas
Waste heat recovery: target 49% of the heat in exhaust gas at 600 to 1,000 °C, leaving flue gas at 250 to 300 °C
Skin temperature: target 110 °C on the ceiling and 85 °C on side walls
Excess air and cold air leaking in through openings and poor seals
Hot walls from thin or damaged insulation
Exhaust heat that no recuperator recovers
Holding the furnace hot while the press waits

example.title: Example: an oil-fired forging furnace (illustrative)
lines: Furnace oil used in the month: 9,000 litres
9,000 / 100 = 90 litres per tonne, inside the 70 to 100 range but near the top
example.note: Figures are illustrative; use your own logbook and weighbridge records.

senseible: Senseible reads your fuel invoices and electricity bills into monthly energy totals. Add your production figures and you get energy per tonne to set against these benchmarks, month after month.
